b1-unit-38.38.1 Life as an expat:
Danny: Hi everyone, and welcome back to Gap Year Diaries! Today's episode is a bit personal. I've been living in São Paulo for several months now, and a lot of you ask me what it's really like to be an expat here. So here's my honest answer.
Danny: The good part first. People here are incredibly friendly, the food is amazing, and some things, like haircuts and eating out, cost a lot less than back home. I'm discovering a new culture, and my Portuguese is getting better every week.
Danny: The hard part? Paperwork. Before I came, I had no idea how many documents I'd need. You need a tax number for lots of things, like opening a bank account, and every office asks for a photocopy of your passport. I carry three copies in my backpack now!
Danny: And some days I feel homesick. I wish my family lived closer. I wish I could have dinner with my mom on Sundays. And honestly, I wish I spoke better Portuguese. When people talk fast, I still get lost. Oh, and I wish people wouldn't switch to English when they hear my accent. I want to practice!
Danny: So, if you're thinking about moving to another country, here are my three tips. Learn a few key phrases before you go. Get health insurance. And give yourself time to get used to the customs. It doesn't happen in a week. See you next time!
